chiefComplaint: Breakouts leave tender bumps and dark marks on the cheeks.

historyAnswers.Onset and duration: The change began gradually over several weeks.
historyAnswers.Itch versus pain: Tender inflammatory lesions; no deep pain or systemic symptoms.
historyAnswers.New medications: No new medication in the past two months.
historyAnswers.Sun exposure and tanning: Outdoor exposure is intermittent; no tanning bed use.
historyAnswers.Personal and family skin cancer history: No personal skin cancer; family history reviewed.
historyAnswers.Pregnancy and contraception status: Review pregnancy possibility and goals before recommending a retinoid or other potentially harmful medication.
historyAnswers.Focused clue: The eruption has fluctuated for months and worsens around menses; ask about scarring, distress, and current products.

acceptableTreatments.name: topical retinoid + benzoyl peroxide
acceptableTreatments.reason: adapalene and benzoyl peroxide; assess pregnancy plans before retinoid counseling

unacceptableTreatments.name: High-potency topical corticosteroid on face or folds
unacceptableTreatments.reason: Site-related atrophy risk; choose site-appropriate treatment.

unacceptableTreatments.name: Systemic corticosteroid for an undifferentiated rash
unacceptableTreatments.reason: May obscure diagnosis and worsen some infections.

unacceptableTreatments.name: Methotrexate without baseline assessment
unacceptableTreatments.reason: Requires screening, labs, pregnancy precautions, and specialist oversight.

unacceptableTreatments.name: Biologic therapy without infection screening
unacceptableTreatments.reason: Requires appropriate screening and specialist plan.

unacceptableTreatments.name: Spironolactone without pregnancy and contraindication review
unacceptableTreatments.reason: Review pregnancy goals, relevant contraindications, and monitoring before use.

unacceptableTreatments.name: Isotretinoin without pregnancy prevention steps when applicable
unacceptableTreatments.reason: Major teratogenic risk; follow current prescribing safeguards.

teachingPearl: Comedones distinguish acne from rosacea; choose therapy by lesion type, severity, scarring risk, and pregnancy goals.
traps: Anchoring on morphology without asking about timing
Using a potent topical steroid on thin or intertriginous skin
Missing medication timing or mucosal symptoms
Ordering biopsy without a decision-changing question
